title: A Relativistic Version of the Ghirardi-Rimini-Weber Model
relevance: The central relativistic-collapse model of flash (GRWf) type: Lorentz-covariant stochastic collapse with local beables (flashes) and NO preferred foliation. Anchor for the 'collapse without foliation is possible' claim.
limits: Full text read at argument level; equations not re-derived. The original lane record did not pin the arXiv version used for its ar5iv extraction; the current citation is pinned to v2 because that version was directly checked in this integration pass, not as a claim about the original extraction. Non-interacting restriction means the model is not a complete relativistic collapse theory of the real world.
section_locator: Original lane read was through an ar5iv HTML rendering (63,608 chars extracted), but its exact arXiv version was not recorded. Subsequent targeted primary-text check used arXiv v2 HTML (https://arxiv.org/html/quant-ph/0406094v2), which identifies v2 dated 16 Sep 2006: abstract; Sec. 3.3 “Law of the Flashes”; Sec. 3.4 “Hyperboloids and Cauchy Surfaces”; Sec. 3.5 “Nonlocality”; Sec. 4 distribution formulas; Sec. 5 “The Temporal Picture”; conclusion. These sections support the no-preferred-slicing and non-interacting-scope statements.
assumptions: N non-interacting spin-1/2 Dirac particles in Minkowski or well-behaved curved spacetime; multi-time wave function on spacelike configurations; jumps of the wave function centered at spacetime points with rate as defined in the paper; primitive ontology = set of flash points.
conclusion: Authors' claim: a Lorentz-invariant (in the sense of covariant law + invariant predictions) spontaneous-collapse model exists without a preferred slicing; it violates Bell inequalities yet reproduces quantum probabilities for all presently testable cases, with in-principle testable deviations; works on curved backgrounds.
proof_status: Mathematical construction with proofs of equivalence of three descriptions (iterative/foliation-free, covariant, foliation-based Markov); not reproduced here. Model limited to non-interacting particles; interacting case requires creation/annihilation and is explicitly out of scope (paper's own statement). The versioned v2 full-text check supports the locators above; the original reader's exact ar5iv version remains undocumented in the preserved pre-repair snapshot (research/redteam/source-repairs/before-records.jsonl, knowledge/preferred-foliation/sources.jsonl line 1).
open_questions: Interacting relativistic GRWf; empirical parameter window against the collapse tests below; whether 'no foliation' blocks or only reframes relativity-of-simultaneity arguments for ontology.
paper_claim_vs_established: Model existence = published result with explicit equations (author claim; construction checked at full-text read, not reproduced). 'No preferred foliation needed' = author claim confirmed in the text. Philosophical reading (flashes as objective happenings without a global now) = our note, not the paper's.

relevance: No-go-style result bounding the whole family: an indeterministic Markovian relativistic collapse dynamics is impossible with only standard degrees of freedom (fields with forward-light-cone spectral condition); stable vacuum + relativistic causality force determinism unless the theory adds nonstandard DOF.
limits: Abstract read only; the proof and precise definitions of 'standard/nonstandard degrees of freedom' not checked.

title: Can Bohmian mechanics be made relativistic?
relevance: Central modern statement of the Bohmian foliation problem and the main escape route: instead of positing a preferred foliation as extra structure, let it be covariantly determined by the wave function; authors argue such theories 'seem to qualify as fundamentally Lorentz invariant'.
limits: Full text read at argument level; Sec. 6 quantum equilibrium skimmed, not re-derived.
section_locator: Read via ar5iv HTML (50,983 chars). Sec. 2 'Bohmian theories in relativistic space-time'; Sec. 3 geometry of foliations (incl. the integrable-vector-field construction where leaves are normal to n only when n is integrable); Sec. 4 'Lorentz invariance'; Sec. 5 generalizations; Sec. 7 'Discussion'.
assumptions: Relativistic Bohmian particle dynamics for N>1 needs a foliation; the question is its status: posited (hero) vs covariantly wave-function-determined; quantum equilibrium assumed for empirical equivalence.
conclusion: Authors' claim: positing a foliation looks like a violation of fundamental Lorentz invariance, but a wave-function-determined foliation yields Bohmian theories that arguably remain fundamentally Lorentz invariant; conclusion is hedged ('seem to qualify').
proof_status: Conceptual/geometric construction with technical sections; main conclusion is explicitly evaluative, not a theorem. Not reproduced. This record pins the audited v2 (24 Dec 2013); exact version is verified in knowledge/audits/fulltext-spotcheck/physics/findings.jsonl, source_id fol-dgtz-2014-can-bohmian. The earlier record snapshot is preserved in research/redteam/source-repairs/before-records.jsonl (knowledge/preferred-foliation/sources.jsonl line 18).
open_questions: Whether wave-function-determined foliations are dynamically stable under interactions; whether 'fundamental Lorentz invariance' under their definition matches philosophical standards for Lorentz invariance.
paper_claim_vs_established: Foliation as extra structure for N>1 = consensus in the Bohmian literature. 'Covariantly wave-function-determined foliation preserves fundamental Lorentz invariance' = the authors' hedged claim, not an established result. Whether this blocks Rietdijk-Putnam-style inference = our note.
